transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Avery (Redwood SE), Miles (Redwood SE), Priya (Ceres Head ML), Samir (Ceres SRE), Lily (Ceres Platform)

Summary:
Short technical deep dive focused on quantization strategies (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ), observed accuracy regressions on Ceres' fine-tuned models, and practical benchmarking for Redwood Private on their on-prem A100 cluster. Action items and benchmark plan agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Priya: Yeah loud and clear, thanks.
[00:12] Avery: Cool, we'll jump straight in. Agenda is quantization tradeoffs, a few examples of regression you shared, and benchmarking plan for VPC/on-prem.
[00:21] Samir: Sounds good. Our main ask is: how aggressive can we go without losing the NLU quality on our inference slice, and what's the perf upside on our A100s.
[00:30] Miles: Right, and also how does the KV cache interact with quantized kernels — we saw a weird latency blip when cache hits were high.
[00:39] Priya: I posted two failing prompts in the doc, one shows hallucination after GPTQ conversion.
[00:45] Jordan: Ok, we'll cover GPTQ/GPT-q... G-P-T-Q and AWQ differences, and where INT8 or FP8 fits. Quick primer: INT8 is usually best for throughput/cost, FP8 gives better dynamic range for some layers, GPTQ is a post-training quant method that can give near-PTQ accuracy with minimal retrain, AWQ is newer with per-channel calibration that can help on LLMs.
[01:10] Priya: Sorry, AWQ? Is that the one that does adaptive weights quant?
[01:15] Avery: Yeah AWQ is adaptive weight quantization, basically per-row/per-channel scaling, often helps on 2-4bit but we see it used for 8-bit too in some stacks. It trades CPU/GPU kernel complexity for accuracy.
[01:27] Lily: If we go GPTQ, do we need a lot of calibration data or does Redwood provide tooling?
[01:32] Jordan: GPTQ needs representative activations; usually a few hundred to a few thousand samples per domain works. We'll share our GPTQ harness and benchmarks.
[01:40] Samir: Our worry is silent regressions — metric stays same but edge cases break. The examples Priya gave are edge intents for our dialog.
[01:47] Avery: Right — we always recommend running prompt-level regressions and per-intent accuracy checks. For GPTQ we often see small token-level divergence that cascades in generative tasks.
[01:55] Priya: Do you have guidance on INT8 vs FP8 for Mistral-ish architectures? Our backbone is a 20B model with RMSnorm + SwiGlu.
[02:04] Miles: Mistral-type archs can be sensitive in certain matmul blocks; FP8 sometimes preserves behavior in GELU/Swiglu variants. But INT8 gives bigger perf wins on the runtime.
[02:12] Jordan: exact numbers: in our internal runs on RTX/A100, INT8 gave 1.8-2.4x token throughput vs FP16; FP8 gave ~1.5-1.9x but with fewer accuracy regressions on some models. GPTQ almost matches FP16 accuracy with a small perf hit compared to naive INT8.
[02:33] Priya: That's great, can you quantify "small perf hit"?
[02:36] Avery: Typically GPTQ runtime is similar to INT8 for forward once kernels are generated, but the conversion step is heavier. AWQ can be slightly slower at inference because of per-channel scaling, maybe 5-15% slower than a highly-optimized INT8 kernel, depending on kernel fusion.
[02:49] Samir: About KV cache: we saw token latency spike when cache hit rate is >80%. Any idea why?
[02:56] Miles: Two possibilities: 1) the quantized KV layout causes misaligned memory reads forcing extra copies, or 2) runtime falls back to slower kernels on cache miss/hit pattern. We suspect memory alignment.
[03:08] Avery: Also batch packing interacts: with high cache hits, sequence lengths become longer effectively and batching heuristics change, bumping up the execution path.
[03:18] Priya: So on-prem A100, what's the recommended kernel stack? Triton/TensorRT or Redwood's own kernel set?
[03:24] Jordan: For Private we default to Redwood's optimized kernels (we tune for INT8/FP8), but customers can use TensorRT for lower-level control. For your fleet we can run Redwood kernels and compare against TensorRT.
[03:34] Samir: We'd like both numbers. We'll provision a test VPC.
[03:38] Jordan: Great, noted.
[03:41] Priya: Back to accuracy: the hallucination in one of our prompts appears after GPTQ conversion — it inserts incorrect entity names mid-sentence. Could that be quant noise?
[03:50] Avery: Yes, token preference can shift with small changes in logits. GPTQ sometimes introduces micro-shifts in embedding layers or first attention projections which can change beam selection.
[03:58] Miles: Mitigations: 1) per-layer fallback for sensitive layers (keep them FP16), 2) small calibration with in-domain prompts to tune scales, 3) prefix/KV caching strategies to reduce divergence.
[04:11] Priya: Layer fallback — can Redwood runtime do mixed precision per-layer?
[04:14] Jordan: Yep, we support mixed configs per model. You can pin certain layers to FP16 while quantizing the rest. It's a common pattern.
[04:21] Samir: How does that change perf? If we keep first n layers FP16 and rest INT8 what's the hit?
[04:26] Avery: Depends which layers; keeping embedding/projection layers in FP16 typically costs a small percentage of total token time — often 5-15% depending on model depth. We'll provide specific microbenchmarks.
[04:36] Priya: What about caching — does KV cache need to be recomputed or re-quantized?
[04:40] Miles: KV cache stores activations after projection; in quantized runs the cache is stored in the quantized format and used directly. The tricky part is when you have mixed LRU and different precision across replicas, conversions can add overhead.
[04:52] Jordan: Also if you warm the cache with FP16 and then switch to INT8 you need to be careful — best to run consistent precision across a session.
[04:59] Samir: Ok. For benchmarking plan we want: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec for typical dialog load, and regression tests against 300 golden prompts.
[05:07] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll include token-level divergence, perplexity delta, and end-to-end intent accuracy.
[05:12] Priya: On the topic of AWQ — you mentioned it's a bit slower. Does it ever out-perform GPTQ on accuracy?
[05:18] Avery: On some models AWQ can preserve accuracy better than naive GPTQ in low-bit regimes because of per-channel scaling; but GPTQ with a good calibration set often trumps AWQ for 8-bit. For 4-bit AWQ or GPTQ variants vary.
[05:30] Priya: Do you have examples where AWQ produced better NLU?
[05:33] Miles: Yes, on a few generative summarization models with skewed activation distribution AWQ reduced token dropout. We'll share anonymized examples.
[05:41] Samir: Deployment note: we need KMS integration for Private so model weights and quantization artifacts are encrypted at rest. Is that supported?
[05:48] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM for model blobs and audit logs for conversions. We'll share the security pack.
[05:54] Lily: Any recommended rollback strategy if we see regressions post-deploy?
[05:58] Avery: Canary with automatic fallback is best — Redwood can route a percentage of traffic to FP16 variants and abort rollout based on eval metrics.
[06:06] Priya: For our pilot, can we start with a mixed approach: GPTQ on most layers, keep attention projections FP16, and run AWQ as an alternate run?
[06:13] Jordan: That sounds sensible. We'll produce two variants: GPTQ-mixed and AWQ-variant and run A/B on the pilot.
[06:18] Samir: One more low-level: do your INT8 kernels use symmetric or asymmetric quant? We saw odd bias shifts.
[06:24] Miles: Our kernels support per-tensor symmetric and per-channel asymmetric. We often recommend per-channel asymmetric for weights to reduce bias.
[06:33] Priya: Good to know. Also latency targets: we need p95 < 350ms for 128-token sequences under 50 qps. Achievable?
[06:40] Avery: On A100, with INT8 and batching tuned, we expect p95 ~200-300ms, depending on request heterogeneity and cache hit ratios. We'll test with your trace.
[06:50] Jordan: We'll run with your sample traffic; if we can't meet SLO with INT8 we'll try FP8 or mixed fallback to hit quality targets.
[06:57] Priya: Are there any known gotchas when converting fine-tuned models rather than base models?
[07:02] Miles: Fine-tunes can amplify small quant shifts. Also adapters or LoRA layers sometimes need special handling — quantizing LoRA separately or keeping adapters in FP16 often helps.
[07:12] Priya: Our models use LoRA for rapid iterations, so that's important.
[07:15] Jordan: Noted — we'll include LoRA guidance and a script to isolate adapter layers during conversion.
[07:21] Samir: For the benchmark harness, can Redwood run everything in our VPC so we can observe network impacts?
[07:26] Jordan: Yes, Private mode can run in your VPC. We'll connect and run harnesses onsite.
[07:31] Lily: We care about observability — token-level cost and latency breakdown. Does Redwood console show per-route model-level metrics?
[07:38] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route token cost, p50/p95 latency, and model-level traces. We'll grant you a demo account.
[07:44] Priya: Great. Anything else on regression detection?
[07:47] Avery: We recommend a test suite with golden prompts + automated evaluation for semantic similarity (embedding-based) and task-specific metrics. Also synthetic stress tests for long context churns.
[07:58] Samir: Ok that covers it. Let's recap next steps...
[08:01] Jordan: Recap: Jordan shares GPTQ/AWQ benchmark sheet + examples (10/12), Avery runs INT8 latency sweep on your A100 (10/14), Samir to set up VPC and provide trace (10/11). We'll prepare two model bundles for pilot: GPTQ-mixed and AWQ-variant.
[08:17] Priya: Thanks everyone, look forward to the results.
[08:20] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up in the doc.

Notes on transcription quality: ASR occasionally munges acronyms (G-P-T-Q typed as G P T Q), and some technical terms like SwiGlu/GELU are imperfectly transcribed.
